name: Theo Von
note: STAGE PERSONA graph for the 'Why is X Funny?' video series. Graph-only. Hypothesis unless sets measured. Stage persona only.

identity.deal: Louisiana swamp philosopher who delivers the dumbest profound thing in a drawl until you're not sure which it is.
identity.premise: A man who sounds like he failed upward into wisdom and treats every modern inconvenience as a parable from the bayou.
identity.awareness_note: Semi: the goof is played straight; the wisdom is either accidental or too good to be accidental.

philosophy.ontology: The world is a series of animals wearing people clothes.
philosophy.epistemology: If it sounds like a saying your uncle made up, it's probably true.
philosophy.axiology: Being kind beats being right; being weird beats both.
philosophy.causality: One small road story becomes a cosmology if you let it.
philosophy.agency: Anyone can be smart; almost nobody can be honestly confused out loud.

dramatic_core.want: to understand one true thing about being a person
dramatic_core.fear: sounding like a guy who read a book instead of a guy who lived a life
dramatic_core.need: the room to laugh with him at the strangeness
dramatic_core.self_model: a guy who took a wrong turn at the interstate and found wisdom
blind_spots: the goof can become a cage
the drawl can hide how sharp the observation is

identity.misinterpretation_rule: Treats modern life as a foreign country he's reporting from with the wrong map, and the wrong map is funnier and sometimes truer.
contradictions: the party guy with the poet's eye
the goof who lands the deepest line
the podcast machine who still sounds like he just woke up

status_model.desired_status: the weird uncle you actually listen to
status_model.felt_status: a man permanently mid-double-take at the modern world

expression.emotional_restraint: medium — the eyes do the thinking
tells: the long pause before the weird image
the 'you know what it is' opener
the sudden precise metaphor in a swamp of words

threads: modern life as a foreign country
the drawl as a delivery system
problem_space: the body as a funny animal
identity.style_thesis: Swamp-philosopher engine: treats modern life as a foreign country he's reporting from with the wrong map — and the wrong map is funnier and sometimes truer. The goof-to-wisdom ratio is the engine: the room is laughing at the goof when the wisdom lands, and the wisdom hits harder because they were laughing.

essay_seeds.title: Theo Von: 'The road story / small-town parable' — how the bit works
essay_seeds.thesis: One small road story becomes a cosmology if you let it. The structure is parable: concrete image → unexpected universal. The drawl sells the sincerity; the observation is too precise to be accidental.
outline: what this reveals about the engine

essay_seeds.title: Theo Von: 'Animals in people clothes' — how the bit works
essay_seeds.thesis: Treats people as animals wearing costumes (literalise) and describes the animal behavior with deadpan precision. The room recognizes the animal first, the person second — that order is the joke.
outline: what this reveals about the engine

internal.cite: Attardo & Raskin — General Theory of Verbal Humor
internal.claim: Joke = {SO, LM, SI, TA, NS, LA}. Technique and Narrative Strategy shape how the mechanism is staged.

internal.cite: Attardo & Pickering 2011 — Timing in the performance of jokes
internal.claim: Punch lines preceded by substantial pauses (0.6-0.8s+); timing = pause distribution + speech rate.

internal.cite: arxiv 2605.00143 — Timing is Everything: Temporal Scaffolding of Semantic Surprise in Humor
internal.claim: Temporal features substantially outweigh semantic incongruity for audience appreciation; timing GATES cognitive access.
Humor from the detection and resolution of an incongruity between expected and actual.
Something is funny when it is a violation (wrong, threatening, unsettling) AND benign (safe, acceptable, play-framed).

internal.cite: Roger & Duffy / status theory of humor
internal.claim: Humor often involves the fall of status or the reversal of a status hierarchy.
Audience and performer share knowledge the persona pretends not to have; the laugh is the alliance signal.

internal.cite: Norrick 2004 — Co-operative principle in conversational joking
internal.claim: Humor escalates by building on prior material, violating cooperative expectations of relevance/quantity.
